page: Amazon Web Services i3en.metal is a bare-metal storage-optimized server designed for high-throughput, data-intensive workloads. It is powered by a 48-core, 96-thread Intel Xeon 8259CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture operating at 3.1 GHz. Without hypervisor overhead, it provides direct physical access to the underlying hardware, which includes 768 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, and an integrated local storage capacity of 60,000 GB spread across low-latency NVMe SSDs. Dedicated hardware resources ensure predictable low latency and eliminate multi-tenant contention.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel compute, memory, and I/O capabilities. In multi-threaded workloads, the system achieved a stress-ng score of 81,867.78 and a PassMark CPU score of 57,184.5, placing it in the top quartile of tested hardware. Memory throughput is equally robust, reaching 224.36 GB/sec for uncached read operations. The high-speed NVMe array and memory capacity translate directly into strong database performance, demonstrated by a PassMark database score of 22,150.5 and 77.09 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics remain moderate, with Geekbench 6 single-core scoring 1,327.0, and CPU-based LLM token generation performs poorly due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, i3en.metal delivers exceptional resource density by pairing high vCPU counts with substantial RAM and 60 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage. Organizations needing dense local storage avoid the overhead and variable latency of network-attached block storage. These hardware attributes make the server well matched for distributed non-relational databases, large-scale search clusters, big data analytics engines, and high-concurrency in-memory data stores that require high network and storage throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services i3en.metal is a storage-optimized bare-metal server configured with 48 physical cores and 96 virtual cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. Lacking hypervisor abstraction, the instance provides direct access to 768 GB of DDR4 memory, 100 Gbps network bandwidth, and 60,000 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. In synthetic evaluations, the platform demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing and I/O throughput, highlighted by a multi-core stress-ng score of 81,867.78, 77.09 million Redis SET operations per second, and strong database transaction execution. However, single-thread performance is modest, and token generation on deep learning tasks is constrained by CPU execution. The platform is engineered specifically for massive data operations, including distributed databases, big data analytics, Elasticsearch indexing, and real-time transaction processing.
